SOURCE: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning without Prompting. Xuezhi Wang, Denny Zhou (Google DeepMind). arXiv:2402.10200v2, 23 May 2024 (preprint).
COVERAGE: 74,616 of 74,616 chars, 23 of 23 pages (main text, related work, limitations, appendices A-D, tables 8-13). References skimmed only. Figures 3, 4, 5 and 6 are bar and line charts with no extractable numbers. I did not run the figures script.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. CoT-decoding takes the top-k first tokens, continues each greedily, and picks the path whose answer tokens have the highest top-1 minus top-2 probability margin. This beats greedy and every other decoding baseline when no prompt is used.
 number: GSM8K 9.9% to 25.1% (Mistral-7B pretrained); 34.8% to 63.2% (PaLM-2 L)
 setup: "Q: [question]\nA:" format, k=10 at the first decoding position, greedy afterwards. Pretrained models, GSM8K test set, no CoT prompt.
 quote: "Greedy decoding 9.9% 34.8% / Self-consistency without CoT-prompt (10 paths) 12.9% 40.6% / CoT-decoding (10 paths) 25.1% 63.2%"
 where: Table 3, p.5
2. Other decoders do not help. Sampling and beam search are worse than greedy without a CoT prompt.
 number: top-k sampling 4.9, nucleus 6.4, beam 6.7, temp 0.7 7.5, greedy 9.9, self-consistency 12.9, CoT-decoding 25.1
 setup: Mistral-7B pretrained, GSM8K, k=10, p=0.9, beam b=10
 quote: "Top-𝑘 sampling (𝑘 = 10) 4.9% / Top-𝑝 / Nucleus sampling (𝑝 = 0.9) 6.4% / Beam search (𝑏 = 10) 6.7% / Temperature sampling (𝑇 = 0.7) 7.5% / Greedy decoding 9.9%"
 where: Table 4, p.6
3. The answer-confidence margin picks CoT paths better than model probability or length-normalised probability.
 number: GSM8K (top-100 questions) greedy 44.0, best raw log-prob 37.0, length-normalised 51.0, CoT-decoding 72.0. Year parity 57.0, 55.0, 57.0, 95.0.
 setup: PaLM-2 L, 10 paths. Also, on the first 100 GSM8K questions the highest-confidence path of the top 10 contained a CoT in 88% of cases.
 quote: "CoT-decoding (decode 10 paths, rank by model’s answer confidence)72.0% 95.0%" and "among those, if we take the decoding path with the highest answer confidence among the top-10 decoding paths, 88% of them contain CoT paths"
 where: Table 2, p.5 (88% claim p.4)
4. Combined with a zero-shot CoT prompt, CoT-decoding with weighted path aggregation beats self-consistency. Cost is O(k).
 number: Mistral-7B / PaLM-2 L on GSM8K: zero-shot CoT 17.5 / 75.1; self-consistency + zero-shot CoT 39.4 / 85.3; CoT-decoding agg + zero-shot CoT 48.4 / 87.0; max-path + zero-shot CoT 40.2 / 78.6. Without a prompt, agg 25.3 / 64.1.
 setup: GSM8K test set, k=10 for every multi-path method. Aggregation picks the answer maximising the sum of Δ over paths with that answer.
 quote: "CoT-decoding (agg path) + zero-shot CoT-prompt48.4% 87.0% O( 𝑘)"
 where: Table 7, p.10
5. Gains across instruction-tuned models are smaller but present.
 number: Mistral-7B inst-tuned: GSM8K 31.2 to 38.2; MultiArith 37.8 to 66.5; year parity 62.2 to 73.5. Pretrained: GSM8K 9.9 to 25.1; MultiArith 14.3 to 45.7; year parity 35.0 to 66.0.
 quote: "MultiArith Greedy 14.3 37.8CoT-decoding 45.7 (+31.4) 66.5 (+28.7)"
 where: Table 5, p.8
6. Pretrained PaLM-2 L with CoT-decoding nearly matches the instruction-tuned model, and gains hold across scales.
 number: 63.2% vs 67.8% (GSM8K); "+10-30% absolute" on GSM8K across PaLM-2 sizes; year parity "almost perfect accuracy at larger model scales" while greedy stays flat with scale.
 quote: "CoT-decoding achieves 63.2% accuracy on the pre-trained PaLM-2 Large model, close to the performance of the instruction-tuned model of the same scale at 67.8%"
 where: p.7 (Fig 4)
7. Gains shrink as synthetic tasks get harder. Correct CoT paths are rare at 3 or more steps. In some cases the few-shot CoT prompt acts as "teaching".
 number: PaLM-2 L, greedy to CoT-decoding. Coin flip 2/3/4 rounds: 70.0 to 94.0, 53.0 to 57.0, 48.0 to 55.0. Web of lies 3/4/5: 76.0 to 87.0, 58.0 to 63.0, 53.6 to 57.6. Multi-step arithmetic d2,l4: 0.0 to 16.0. Sports understanding 58.8 to 58.0 (slightly worse). Object counting 36.0 to 39.2.
 setup: 100 generated examples per difficulty level (Web-of-Lies 5 uses the existing BBH data).
 quote: "models can generate the correct CoT paths when the solution involves at most 1 or 2 step knowledge manipulation, and the model starts to struggle with generating the correct CoT-paths when the steps become 3 or more"
 where: Table 6, p.9
8. CoT paths are usually not the top-ranked or majority path, so majority vote fails. Branching at the first token gives the most diversity.
 number: none (qualitative)
 quote: "they often do not represent the predominant answer among all paths, rendering methods like self-consistency (Wang et al., 2023a) inapplicable"
 where: p.4. Also p.5-6: "early branching, e.g., at the first decoding step, significantly enhances the diversity of potential paths". Sampling fails without a prompt because "the model’s strong tendency in providing a direct answer" makes the first token low-diversity.
9. Larger k helps for pretrained models. For instruction-tuned models the effect is smaller, because CoT paths already sit in the first few paths.
 number: none in text (Fig 5 and 6)
 quote: "higher values of 𝑘 typically result in improved model performance, suggesting that in many cases, the correct CoT paths may indeed exist but are often ranked lower"
 where: p.8
10. Year-parity example: greedy is at chance. Example Δ values for CoT versus non-CoT paths: 0.949 and 0.978 versus 0.117 to 0.207.
 quote: "k = 3: 1964, aneven year. (0.949)"
 where: Table 1, p.3

Settings: PaLM-2 uses input length 256 and max 128 decode steps for CoT-decoding. Few-shot and zero-shot CoT prompting use 1024 input length and 256 output steps. Mistral math generates 200 new tokens (pretrained) or 400 (instruction-tuned). Model IDs: mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1, google/gemma-7b. Mistral year parity ground truth is the model's own recalled birth year. (App. D, p.20-21)

LIMITS
- Authors concede extra compute (k paths). Δ is "less precise" for open-ended answers. Only the first token is branched.
- Not shown: any test on frontier or chat models, any latency or cost figure, any head-to-head with few-shot CoT on GSM8K without a prompt. Models are 2023-24 pretrained (PaLM-2, Mistral-7B v0.1, Gemma-7B).
- Table 7 shows zero-shot CoT prompting alone (75.1% on PaLM-2 L) beats prompt-free CoT-decoding (63.2%). The decoding trick matters for pretrained models and for studying intrinsic ability, not as a replacement for prompting.
- Needs token-level logprobs and control of the first decoding step, which most hosted APIs do not offer. This is my inference, not stated in the paper.
- Sports Understanding fell slightly (58.8 to 58.0).
- Answer extraction relies on heuristics (last number, or the continuation after "So the answer is"). Ill-formed outputs are filtered.
- The paper does not compare against a plain "think step by step" prompt on pretrained models other than in Table 7.

BUILDS ON: Wei et al. 2022 (few-shot CoT); Kojima et al. 2022 (zero-shot CoT, "So the answer is"); Wang et al. 2023a (self-consistency); Jiang and Gupta 2019 (min-margin uncertainty); Cobbe et al. 2021a (GSM8K); Allen-Zhu and Li 2023 (year parity / knowledge manipulation); Chung et al. 2022 (instruction tuning with CoT); Suzgun et al. 2022 (BBH); McCoy et al. 2023 (pretraining distribution effects).

CODE: none. The only formula is the confidence measure: Δ_{k,answer} = (1/|answer|) Σ_{x_t∈answer} [p(x_t^1 | x_<t) − p(x_t^2 | x_<t)] (p.4). The aggregation score is Δ̃_a = Σ_k Δ_{k,a}. Worked example in Table 9: the correct answer 18 has Δ = 0.994, 0.911, 0.584 and 0.999 (sum 3.5).

FIGURES (captions only, no images viewed)
- Fig 1 (p.2): the apples example, greedy gives "5" while paths 2 and 4 give "8" with higher certainty. This is the fastest way to explain the idea.
- Fig 2 (p.5): branching at later decoding steps.
- Fig 3: accuracy gains on PaLM-2, Mistral and Gemma across three tasks.
- Fig 4 (p.7): GSM8K and year parity accuracy by PaLM-2 scale, greedy vs CoT-decoding.
- Fig 5: effect of k. Fig 6 (App. C): k on Mistral.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean apart from missing spaces and garbled math symbols. Chart values for Figs 3-6 are not extractable. Table 3 and Table 4 share the same figures (12.9 and 25.1). No embedded instructions found. For note 03-core-techniques: this is a decoding method, not a prompt technique. The paper's usable prompt-side finding is that prompt-free greedy is weak on reasoning, and that zero-shot CoT with CoT-decoding stacks to 87.0% on PaLM-2 L.
